title: transitiontrees — Design Conventions
text: transitiontrees fitted variable-depth context tree: list nodes keyed pathway string flat edges data.frame traversal alphabet, fit hyperparameters, pruned flag class: c("transitiontrees") Everything else package function consumes transitiontrees returns either: another transitiontrees (e.g. prune()), tidy data.frame (pathway-centric API), scalar / numeric vector (scoring), graphics object (plotting).

title: transitiontrees — Design Conventions
text: Plural collections, singular one thing. Nouns collide sibling packages get transitiontrees_ prefix:

title: transitiontrees — Design Conventions
text: Always data.frame (tibble — keep base-R ). Column order: Plain-English column names (renamed original modal_next/prob_next/KL/flips readability). divergence Kullback-Leibler divergence parent context’s prediction; changes_prediction modal-flip flag. Sorted leading numeric column (count tree_pathways(), divergence divergent_pathways, next_probability sharp_pathways). Sort direction descending unless column length / cost. empty case returns schema-stable 0-row data.frame columns. Argument values use canonical names : sort_by takes c("count", "divergence", "depth"); bootstrap_pathways(stat=) takes c("count", "next_probability", "divergence") (plus "G2" plot_pathway_resamples()). tree_dependence() extends entropy (Shannon entropy next-state distribution), entropy_before (parent’s entropy), entropy_drop (entropy_before - entropy), likely_before (parent’s likely next state) support information-theoretic diagnostics. compare_trees()’s breakdown uses count_a, count_b, divergence_ab, divergence_ba, divergence_sym; bootstrap_pathways() uses leading schema plus mean_divergence / ci_divergence_* / M_divergence etc.
code: pathway | depth | count | likely_next | next_probability | divergence | changes_prediction

title: transitiontrees — Design Conventions
text: tune_tree() returns data.frame one row per grid point: smoothing rendered label ("floor", "floor(ymin=0.001)", "kneser_ney(discount=0.5)", …) multi-method hyperparameter-sweep grids unambiguous one column. n_nodes_avg mean tree size across folds (post-prune size prune = TRUE). folds_failed counts CV folds errored configuration. Sorted perplexity ascending; attr(grid, "best") exposes minimum-perplexity row among configurations whose every fold scored (folds_failed == 0 finite perplexity), NULL none qualify — failed configuration never reported best.
code: max_depth | nmin | smoothing | prune | logLik | n_scored | perplexity | n_nodes_avg | folds_failed

title: transitiontrees — Design Conventions
text: Scalar: logLik(tree, newdata), perplexity(tree, newdata). One-call bundle: model_fit(tree, newdata = NULL) returns tidy one-row data.frame (logLik | df | nobs | AIC | BIC | perplexity), --sample newdata given, one row per group transitiontrees_group. Per-sequence: score_sequences(tree, newdata) returns data.frame sequence_id, n_scored, log_lik, perplexity — n_scored rather n_obs positions whose observed state outside training alphabet dropped score, counted obs. Per-position: score_positions(tree, newdata) returns data.frame sequence_id, position, matched_context, observed, predicted_prob, log_lik.

title: transitiontrees — Design Conventions
text: context_tree(..., smoothing = c("floor", "laplace", "kneser_ney", "witten_bell", "jelinek_mercer")) "interpolate" (default) — interpolating rule: distribution zero-count state shifted toward uniform, p_i = (1 - k*ymin)*p_i + ymin, zero lands exactly ymin; fully observed distributions stay raw MLE. gives full-depth machine-precision parity external reference (see PARITY.md). "cap" — original transitiontrees rule: clamp every probability ymin renormalise. Opt-via list("floor", ymin = .., rule = "cap"). "laplace" — additive-α; alpha argument, default 1 "kneser_ney" — back-along suffix path discount D continuation probabilities; canonical prediction suffix trees (Begleiter, El-Yaniv & Yona 2004 §3); discount argument, default 0.75 "witten_bell" — interpolation novelty-based weight "jelinek_mercer" — fixed-λ interpolation order-k order-(k-1); lambda argument Smoothing applied context_tree(). Re-smoothing fitted tree smooth_tree(tree, smoothing) — returns new tree.

title: transitiontrees — Design Conventions
text: Four accepted shapes: Wide character matrix data.frame (rows = sequences, columns = time-steps). NAs allowed; trailing NAs treated end--sequence. List character vectors (element one ragged sequence). NAs allowed inside. 1 2, missing cells (NA "") dropped sequence — whether trailing internal — leaving observed states order; gap closed, never coerced literal "NA" state. shapes share one cleaning rule (.ct_clean_seq) identical data yields identical tree regardless container. sequence kept long ≥ 1 observed state (contributes root marginal even admits transition). stslist — extracted via .matrix(stslist); alphabet honoured; weights honoured present. fitted transition/network object, taken directly — auto-detected S3 class (e.g. netobject (c("netobject", "cograph_network")), cograph_network, tna). Detection class structurally (list-like object exposing 2-D $data/$sequences/$seqdata slot), future sibling follows convention needs code change. state-label map resolved across conventions — $nodes id/label table, positional $labels, labels/alphabet attribute — integer-coded frame decoded . object accepted : sequence frame extracted wherever upstream kept — $data first (documented handoff), $sequences / $seqdata / "data"/"sequences" attribute / embedded netobject — caller need know storage slot. frame non-empty wide trailing-NA-padded frame (one row per session), either character integer-coded: integer-coded frame decoded $nodes id/label table (label[match(code, id)]), NA preserved — rejected. Positional $labels read 1-based (code k = state k); 0 otherwise --range code, id-table code absent $nodes, explicit error, silent drop/recycle. “reject numeric matrices” rule disambiguates top-level square transition matrix apply inside contractual sequence slot (object’s transition matrix lives $weights, $data). $nodes$label (network’s canonical node set) becomes default alphabet unless caller passes one explicitly. sequence unit whatever upstream builder’s session= defined; encoded object, re-chosen . contract boundary sibling network packages: network object handoff format. Unwrapping happens row-count / weight detection see frame, raw slot list. network object carries $data sequences (pure graph: nodes/edges/weights — .e. aggregated transition network) rejected explicit, instructive error, silently coerced. original sequences recovered edge weights — invariant numeric-matrix rejection , applied object form. Grouped inputs. grouped family object (netobject_group / group_tna), named list whose every element single family object, fits one tree per element returns transitiontrees_group. Equivalently, single dataset plus group = ($metadata column name network object, vector one entry per sequence) split batch-fitted. groups share one alphabet (union, explicit alphabet =) trees stay comparable. grouped object passed single object expected detected class structurally — silently mistaken ragged list. Numeric matrices accepted input — collide “square numeric matrix = transition matrix” network-toolkit ecosystem. Numeric inputs must cast character explicitly. guiding rule pure-graph case: transitiontrees fits sequences, never aggregated transitions.

title: transitiontrees — Design Conventions
text: plot.transitiontrees(tree, style = c("horizontal", "dendrogram", "icicle", "interactive")): "horizontal" (default) — pure-ggplot2 left--right phylogram. Root left, depth increasing rightward, smooth curved branches, leaf labelled full arrow-form pathway. Internal-node names sit nodes. optional-package dependency; layout use citing specific pathways inline. "dendrogram" — pure-ggplot2 radial dendrogram. Root centre, leaves outer ring; node size = count, fill = state. optional-package dependency. "icicle" — circular partition (sunburst) drawn pure ggplot2; partition layout computed base R, optional-package dependency. "interactive" — draggable/zoomable hierarchical htmlwidget via visNetwork (Suggests). encoding static styles — node size = count, edge width = child’s count (flow), fill = last state — plus hover tooltips. Errors install hint visNetwork missing. point_size_range / edge_size_range control pixel sizing (defaults c(10, 45) / c(1, 10)). three static styles (horizontal, dendrogram, icicle) carry optional-package dependency, render R context (script, knitr, headless). interactive gates Suggests package (visNetwork) errors install hint absent. plot_pathways() plot_divergence() pathway-centric views complement (don’t replace) tree plot. plot_trajectories(tree, measure = c("frequency", "predictability")) forward complement plot.transitiontrees(): prefix tree follows sequences left--right time, coloured either many sequences walk path ("frequency") model’s  step ("predictability"). Added 2026-06-07 replace bespoke per-analysis plotting code: first-class verb taking tree explicitly (hidden state). Drawn pure ggplot2 (rectangular node glyphs), optional-package dependency.

title: Numerical parity of transitiontrees
text: Reaching full-depth probability parity required matching reference floor smoother exactly. shifts distribution contains zero-count state toward uniform: applied distributions least one zero entry; fully observed distributions stay raw MLE. transitiontrees’s floor now uses rule default (rule = "interpolate"). original transitiontrees rule — clamp probability ymin renormalise — remains available opt-: two rules differ sparse nodes (state zero count) O(ymin); fully observed distributions identical. earlier “machine-precision” claim , fact, validated depth ≤1 (harness bug compared deep contexts mismatched key formats); suite now compares every depth.

title: Numerical parity of transitiontrees
text: prune_tree(criterion = "G2", alpha) reference prune(gain = "G2", C) use likelihood-ratio gain differ two documented ways, now quantified gated configs: Degrees freedom. transitiontrees uses textbook df = k−1 k-category multinomial LRT — keeps child 2·N·KL(child‖parent) > qchisq(1−alpha, k−1). reference compares N·KL (= G²/2) raw cutoff C, worked example sets C95 = qchisq(0.95, 1)/2 — .e. reference hardcodes df = 1. prune_tree(alpha = 0.05) equals reference C = qchisq(.95, k−1)/2, worked example’s C = qchisq(.95, 1)/2, except k = 2 df 1. Empirical vs smoothed + recursion. transitiontrees’s G² uses empirical child distribution (counts/n); reference uses smoothed node prob — O(ymin) difference can flip node sitting exactly cutoff. reference also prunes top-level--level vs transitiontrees’s bottom-collapse, prune unsmoothed (ymin = 0) tree . Measured 30 randomised configs (alphabet 2–4): df = 1 cutoff transitiontrees’s kept set always subset reference’s (never keeps node reference drops), k = 2 two agree exactly. df matched, agreement exact vast majority; residual O(ymin) smoothed-vs-empirical tie-break. Conclusion: two pruners equivalent () df convention (transitiontrees = statistically-correct k−1; reference = hardcoded 1) (b) O(ymin) borderline tie-break — algorithmic divergence.

title: Case study: human-AI collaboration
text: ai_long bundled log coded messages AI-assisted project work, one row per coded move. message can carry several codes, message may occupy several rows. Actor: project — project; 34 projects contribute sessions. Session: session_id — collaboration session, 428 total; session one sequence. Time: timestamp — Unix time seconds; session_date holds date text. Order: order_in_session — position move within session; message_id code_order identify message position code within . Fine state: code — move, one eight codes (Ask, Delegate, Execute, Explain, Investigate, Plan, Repair, Report). Coarse state: cluster — category move: Action (Delegate, Execute, Investigate), Communication (Ask, Explain, Report) Repair (Plan, Repair).

This tna object carries no sequence data anywhere (no usable $data / $sequences / $seqdata / embedded netobject). It looks like a pure graph - an aggregated transition network - and transitiontrees fits on raw sequences, not on aggregated transitions: the original sequences cannot be recovered from edge weights (the same reason numeric transition matrices are rejected). Pass a sequence-bearing object instead, e.g. a wide-format transition/network object that still carries its raw sequences, or the original wide sequence data.frame.

title: Model selection: tuning, fit and perplexity
text: sequence x1,…,xTx_1, \dots, x_T, tree predicts state longest context c*(t)c^*(t) tree ends history . log likelihood set sequences sum predicted positions, ℓ=∑tlog⁡p̃(xt∣c*(t)), \ell = \sum_t \log \tilde p\big(x_t \mid c^*(t)\big), tree |𝒞|(|S|−1)|\mathcal{C}|\,(|S| - 1) free parameters, one distribution |S||S| states |𝒞||\mathcal{C}| contexts. standard generics return quantities. depth-4 tree 82 contexts therefore 82×2=16482 \times 2 = 164 parameters, estimated 1,870 observations. nn predicted states, AIC=−2ℓ+2df\mathrm{AIC} = -2\ell + 2\,\mathrm{df} BIC=−2ℓ+log⁡(n)df\mathrm{BIC} = -2\ell + \log(n)\,\mathrm{df}. model_fit() returns one row, together perplexity, perplexity=exp⁡(−ℓ/n), \mathrm{perplexity} = \exp(-\ell / n), effective number equally likely next states: |S|=3|S| = 3 uniform guess 1 perfect prediction.

code: count_by_hand <- function(sequences, max_depth) {   events <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(sequences)), function(i) {     states <- unname(sequences[i, ])     states <- states[!is.na(states)]     per_depth <- lapply(seq.int(0L, max_depth), function(d) {       positions <- seq_along(states)       positions <- positions[positions > d]       pathway <- vapply(positions, function(t) {         if (d == 0L) "(start)" else           paste(states[seq.int(t - d, t - 1L)], collapse = " -> ")       }, character(1))       data.frame(pathway = pathway, next_state = states[positions])     })     do.call(rbind, per_depth)   })   events <- do.call(rbind, events)   counts <- table(events$pathway, events$next_state)   data.frame(pathway = rownames(counts),              count = as.integer(rowSums(counts)),              as.data.frame.matrix(counts), row.names = NULL) }  contexts_of <- function(hand) {   lapply(hand$pathway, function(p) {     if (identical(p, "(start)")) character(0) else       strsplit(p, " -> ", fixed = TRUE)[[1L]]   }) } hand <- count_by_hand(learners, max_depth = 2L) hand #>                     pathway count Active Average Disengaged #> 1                   (start)   147     64      68         15 #> 2                    Active    60     43      15          2 #> 3          Active -> Active    40     32       7          1 #> 4         Active -> Average    14      8       6          0 #> 5      Active -> Disengaged     2      1       0          1 #> 6                   Average    62     13      41          8 #> 7         Average -> Active    12      5       7          0 #> 8        Average -> Average    36      4      28          4 #> 9     Average -> Disengaged     8      0       6          2 #> 10               Disengaged    15      3       7          5 #> 11     Disengaged -> Active     3      3       0          0 #> 12    Disengaged -> Average     7      0       4          3 #> 13 Disengaged -> Disengaged     5      2       1          2

text: Six hand-counted distributions contain zero, example Active -> Disengaged (one Active, one Disengaged, Average). check default smoother, apply floor rule hand ymin = 0.001 compare tree fitted default smoothing.
code: floor_by_hand <- function(probabilities, ymin) {   states <- setdiff(names(probabilities), "pathway")   p <- as.matrix(probabilities[states])   k <- length(states)   has_zero <- rowSums(p == 0) > 0   p[has_zero, ] <- (1 - k * ymin) * p[has_zero, ] + ymin   data.frame(pathway = probabilities$pathway, p) } smoothed_tree <- context_tree(learners, max_depth = 2L, min_count = 1L) smoothed <- predict(smoothed_tree, newdata = contexts_of(hand), tidy = TRUE) all.equal(subset(smoothed, select = c(Active, Average, Disengaged)),           subset(floor_by_hand(by_hand, ymin = 0.001),                  select = c(Active, Average, Disengaged)),           tolerance = 1e-12) #> [1] TRUE

code: loglik_by_hand <- function(sequences, max_depth, probabilities) {   states_all <- setdiff(names(probabilities), "pathway")   p <- as.matrix(probabilities[states_all])   rownames(p) <- probabilities$pathway   per_sequence <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(sequences)), function(i) {     states <- unname(sequences[i, ])     states <- states[!is.na(states)]     sum(vapply(seq_along(states), function(t) {       d <- min(t - 1L, max_depth)       context <- if (d == 0L) "(start)" else         paste(states[seq.int(t - d, t - 1L)], collapse = " -> ")       log(p[context, states[t]])     }, numeric(1)))   }, numeric(1))   sum(per_sequence) } loglik_by_hand(learners, max_depth = 2L, probabilities = by_hand) #> [1] -99.95 logLik(tree) #> 'log Lik.' -99.95 (df=26) all.equal(loglik_by_hand(learners, max_depth = 2L, probabilities = by_hand),           as.numeric(logLik(tree)), tolerance = 1e-12) #> [1] TRUE

"dendrogram" radial tree root center, node filled state depth adds history. "icicle" sunburst: rings depths, angular width arc proportional summed count deepest histories beneath , fill state ring adds history. "interactive" visNetwork widget draggable nodes tooltip gives node's count full next-state distribution. node-link drawings, node size count history edge width count child history. first three drawings ggplot objects; interactive one htmlwidget. context tree reads backwards time: every history ends moment prediction. forward view, sequences followed first state, use plot_trajectories(). next-state probabilities many pathways compared easily plot_pathways() plot_distributions(), differences two groups plot_difference().

"G2" leaf kept likelihood-ratio statistic counts parent's distribution exceeds chi-square critical value alpha \(k - 1\) degrees freedom (\(k\) states); leaf tested separately, without correction multiple tests. "KL" leaf kept Kullback-Leibler divergence parent, nats, exceeds threshold. "AIC" "BIC" leaf kept log-likelihood, penalized \(2(k - 1)\) \(\log(n)(k - 1)\) (\(n\) leaf's count), better parent's prediction (Akaike, 1974; Schwarz, 1978). probabilities contexts remain changed. returns tree class fewer contexts. see strongly criterion prunes tree, use compare_pruning(); choose pruned unpruned trees held-data, use tune_tree(); draw "G2" decision along suffix chain one pathway, use plot_pruning(). divergence column tree_pathways() bits, whereas "KL" threshold nats; divide threshold nats log(2) read bits.

Four settings decide much history tree uses far trusts sparse histories: maximum depth, minimum count context needs kept, smoothing next-state distributions, whether tree pruned. deeper, less smoothed tree reproduces sequences fitted closely, necessarily predict new sequences better. Held-perplexity measures second property: exponential mean negative log-likelihood per scored transition sequences model seen, can read effective number next states model choosing . fits tree every combination supplied values scores k-fold cross-validation. Folds formed whole sequences, held-sequence contributes transitions fit, every configuration scored folds. selected configuration one lowest held-perplexity among scored every fold; configuration failed fold kept grid never selected. returns grid transitiontrees_tune data frame one row per configuration, lowest held-perplexity first. grid compares settings --sample prediction. describe fit one tree data use model_fit() perplexity(); compare smoothing methods pruning rules one data set without cross-validation use compare_smoothing() compare_pruning().

title: transitiontrees 0.1.6
text: state_frequencies() returns count proportion state (one table per group grouped fit). summary() methods groups trees, two-tree comparisons tuning grids; summary() group comparison now returns one-row summary object print method instead printing returning pathway table invisibly. .data.frame() methods gain argument reach every table result: = "null" permutation null compare_trees(), = "omnibus" = "distance" compare_groups(), = "best" tune_tree() (new method), = "resamples" (stat) bootstrap_pathways(). predict() gains tidy = TRUE, returning one row per history matched context, likely next state full distribution. generate_sequences() simulate() gain tidy = TRUE, returning wide data frame context_tree() accepts. default outputs unchanged. context_tree() accepts object returned tna::prepare_data().

title: transitiontrees 0.1.6
text: column tune_tree() grid holds minimum count now named min_count, matching argument (nmin). tuning configuration whose folds fail now reports logLik, perplexity n_nodes_avg NA (log-likelihood 0). warning includes first fold error. predict() splits history given arrow-notation string ("-> B") states, warns history contains state outside alphabet. Errors warnings carry condition classes (transitiontrees_bad_input, transitiontrees_alphabet_mismatch, transitiontrees_no_data, transitiontrees_weighted_unsupported, transitiontrees_empty_result, transitiontrees_missing_package, warnings transitiontrees_fold_failed, transitiontrees_no_best, transitiontrees_unknown_state, transitiontrees_degenerate_permutation); argument checks use named stopifnot() messages. plot(tune_tree(...)) marks selected configuration facet; plot() bootstrap result longer emits ggplot2 message. plot_pruning() labels use ASCII text, plot draws locale. common_pathways(depth = ) returns consecutive row names. ggplot2 (>= 3.5.0) required.

title: transitiontrees 0.1.6

New vignettes “Variable-order transition trees” “Comparing groups”, package website eight guides (workflow, data input, smoothing pruning, model selection, pathway reliability, prediction scoring, visualization, verification PST) three case studies. previous five vignettes folded . Every example runs unwrapped fixed seeds; examples added print, summary, plot .data.frame methods. _pkgdown.yml left built package.

title: transitiontrees 0.1.2
text: context_tree() fits variable-depth pathway tree (prediction suffix tree; Ron, Singer & Tishby 1996) wide character matrix / data.frame, list character vectors, long event log (actor / time / action / order / session arguments), transition/network object. NA, "", TraMineR codes % (void) * (missing) treated gaps wide / list input. prepare_input() reshapes long event log wide sequence frame (timestamp / session logic), can carry per-sequence metadata reshape via meta. Five smoothing schemes via unified smoothing argument ("floor", "laplace", "kneser_ney", "witten_bell", "jelinek_mercer"); hyperparameters list(method, ...). prune_tree() supports four criteria: likelihood-ratio G2, Kullback-Leibler, AIC, BIC. smooth_tree() re-smooths fitted tree; model_fit() / n_nodes() tidy fit-summary accessors. Grouped fits: context_tree(..., group =) (per-sequence vector column name) fits one tree per group shared alphabet returns transitiontrees_group. block = carries stratifying id (e.g. subject) compare_groups().

text: tune_tree() k-fold cross-validates max_depth, min_count, smoothing, pruning. bootstrap_pathways() reports per-pathway stability informativeness bootstrap CIs. compare_trees() runs permutation test two-tree divergence. compare_groups() compares transitiontrees_group two axes — behavioral (Jensen-Shannon divergence next-state distributions) usage (prevalence) — permutation null (optionally stratified block repeated-measures designs), Benjamini- Hochberg FDR, -group distance matrix. tree_distance() computes count-weighted symmetric KL two trees.

text: plot() transitiontrees offers four styles: "horizontal" (default), "dendrogram", "icicle" (pure ggplot2), plus "interactive" (visNetwork). plot() transitiontrees_group draws one figure per group. plot_pathways(), plot_divergence(), plot_distributions(), plot_predictive(), plot_pathway_resamples(), bootstrap / comparison / tuning plot methods. plot_difference() renders early-vs-late style difference two groups per-context map (Pearson residuals -difference null, raw probability difference) context-tree layout.
